promptState.text: The image is a candid documentary photograph taken inside a small neighbourhood bakery just after sunrise, a medium shot of a young adult woman baker, 29 years old, setting a black steel tray of fresh croissants onto a wooden cooling rack in front of her. She stands at the centre of the frame, her body turned slightly toward camera-left, looking down at the tray with a calm, focused expression, lips together. She has an oval face, warm brown eyes, straight dark brown hair tied into a low bun with a few loose strands falling at her temples, and light olive skin with fine pores and a soft, even tone, a light dusting of flour on her right forearm. She wears a warm orange cotton t-shirt with the sleeves pushed up above the elbows and a heavy charcoal grey canvas apron tied at the waist, printed across the chest with an orange bakery logo in the warm orange of a ripe apricot: at the top a simple round bunny head with two long upright ears as one solid orange shape, below it the word "PIXA" in thick, rounded, bold letters, and under that the small word "BAKERY" in thin, widely spaced orange capitals, the whole logo a matte screen print soaked into the canvas, the weave of the fabric showing through the ink. Both hands hold the two short edges of the tray through thick grey cotton oven cloths. The croissants are deep golden brown with flaky layers, a few crumbs scattered on the tray. Behind her are dark green square wall tiles, a stainless steel deck oven at camera-right with its door half open and a warm orange glow inside, and plain wooden shelves stacked with round sourdough loaves with floury cracked crusts; a small black chalkboard leaning on the middle shelf reads "FRESH BREAD" in white chalk capitals. Cool blue-white daylight from a tall window at camera-left falls across her face and the front of the apron, while the oven's warm glow lights the right edge of her arm and the side of the tray. Shot at chest height with a 50mm lens at f/4, framed from just above her head to her hips, her face, hands and the croissants sharp, the shelves softly out of focus. A clean, high-resolution photograph from a full-frame camera, with smooth, even tonal gradations in the skin and fine natural detail: true-to-life colour, a palette of charcoal, warm orange, deep green and golden brown.

MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 MiniMax H3 Image needs ComfyUI 0.45.0 or newer, the first version with these nodes. On an older ComfyUI the nodes show red: update ComfyUI first.

 Load Diffusion Model

Download minimax_h3_image_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors19.5 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/h3

Create the h3 folder if it does not exist.

 Load CLIP

Download qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors14.6 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

The same text encoder as MiniMax H3 video: if you did Episode 41 you already have it.

 Load VAE

Download minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors1.09 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 License

MiniMax H3 Image has its own license, the MiniMax-H3-Image Community License, separate from the MiniMax H3 video license. Read it and check what it says for your country before you use the model: some countries need a license from MiniMax first.

READ LICENSE MiniMax H3 Image model page 

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

 Nodes Installed from Manager

  • Pixaroma: update to the latest version (these workflows need at least 1.4.250). A node shows red or missing? Update Pixaroma.

Which version is the newest? The Latest Pixaroma version button shows it and what is new in it. The help page has the update steps for every kind of install.

Latest Pixaroma version How to update Pixaroma 

 Something missing?

Each button opens a short video that shows the fix, with the steps written under it.

Red or missing nodes A model file is missing Buttons missing after an update 

 Resources

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel  Ask for help

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

The basic MiniMax H3 Image workflow: write a prompt, press Run, get a 16 megapixel picture in about 20 seconds. MiniMax H3 Image is MiniMax's own picture model. Next to P-H3 Image from Episode 42, its photos look much more like a real camera took them: pores, stray hairs, skin that is not airbrushed.

 Steps

  1. Write your prompt in Prompt Pixaroma.
  2. Pick a size on Sizes Pixaroma. From top to bottom they are 4, 8 and 16 megapixels, three shapes each. The Portrait / Landscape switch turns the shape on its side.
  3. Leave the seed on F to repeat a picture, or switch it to R for a new one each Run.
  4. Press Run.

 Writing a prompt

  1. Write one long description, the way MiniMax's own example does: The image is a candid documentary photograph taken inside ...
  2. Then the subject and what it does, the place, the light and where it comes from, and the camera: daylight from a tall window at camera-left, 50mm lens at f/4.
  3. Words that should appear go in double quotes: a chalkboard reads "FRESH BREAD".
  4. For a photo, end with a clean finish: A clean, high-resolution photograph from a full-frame camera, with smooth, even tonal gradations in the skin. Words like unedited, phone photo, grain gave blotchy skin and a JPG look in our tests.
  5. Skip 8k, masterpiece, best quality: describe what you want to SEE instead.

 Good to know

  • 16 megapixels is the model's best size: MiniMax says so, and our tests agree. At 8 megapixels the same prompt gave blotchy skin and a JPG look when we zoomed in to 100 %. Below 4 megapixels it does not work well, so the list starts there.
  • A new seed changes the whole picture: the pose, the framing and the room. Look at a few seeds at full size. In our four test seeds one drew the chalkboard twice and one gave her a much too thick arm.
  • The 6 steps are fixed, and there is no CFG and no negative prompt. More steps made the skin worse in our tests.
  • Words in double quotes came out right on every test seed, also the small "BAKERY" on the apron.
  • The model does not know your logo or your character: describe what you see. The bunny logo on the apron is drawn only from the words in the prompt.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 Image) - MiniMax H3 Image, the picture model made by MiniMax itself. It is a different file from the H3 video models of Episode 41 and from P-H3 Image of Episode 42.
  • Load CLIP (MiniMax H3 text encoder) - Reads your prompt. It is the same Qwen3-VL 32B text encoder as MiniMax H3 video, so if you did Episode 41 you already have it. The type must be minimax.
  • Load VAE (MiniMax H3 Image VAE) - Turns the finished render into the picture. It is made for MiniMax H3 Image, a different file from the H3 video VAE and the P-H3 Image VAE.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Prompt Pixaroma (1. your prompt) - The prompt box. The demo prompt is a full description of the picture: write yours the same way (see How to Use).
  • Sizes Pixaroma (2. picture size) - The picture size. Click a size; the Portrait / Landscape switch turns it on its side. From top to bottom: 4, 8 and 16 megapixels, three shapes each (square, 4:3, 16:9). 16 megapixels is the model's best size; the demo is 16 MP in portrait.
  • Seed Pixaroma (3. fixed or random) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same picture every Run, R (random) a new one each Run. The demo uses seed 1.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • MiniMax H3 Image Conditioning (prompt + size) - Joins the prompt and the size, and makes the empty canvas the picture is painted on.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (no negative prompt) - An empty negative. The model takes no negative prompt, and CFG stays at 1.
  • KSampler (6 steps, CFG 1) - The render: 6 steps, CFG 1, euler and simple, as MiniMax made the model. In our tests 10 steps made skin worse, and the er_sde sampler made it noisy, so leave these as they are.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves the picture) - Saves each picture as PNG into ComfyUI/output/MiniMax H3 Image and shows it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: a smaller picture is faster.

SizeTime
4 megapixelsabout 9 s
8 megapixels9 to 14 s
16 megapixels (the demo)about 20 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 35 GB: 19.5 GB for the model, 14.6 GB for the text encoder and 1 GB for the VAE), so it takes longer. After that they stay in memory, if your PC has enough of it.

 On a smaller card

Start with the 4 megapixel sizes, the first three on Sizes Pixaroma, then go up once a picture looks right.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
